title.narrative: REBUILD Vanuatu (Resilient Earthquake Building Assessment and Infrastructure Linkage Development)

description.narrative: On December 17, 2024, a powerful 7.3 magnitude earthquake struck near Port Vila, Vanuatu’s capital. Within 24 hours, a second 5.5 magnitude quake followed, triggering landslides and devastating infrastructure. Over 80,000 people have been affected, with many losing their homes and essential services. This disaster comes as communities are still recovering from twin cyclones in 2023, compounding the nation’s vulnerability.Vanuatu, home to over 300,000 people across 83 islands, faces frequent earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and extreme weather due to its location on the Pacific Ring of Fire. With limited infrastructure and economic resilience, disaster recovery remains a challenge.In response, UNDP has mobilized early recovery efforts since January, engaging in high-level coordination with government and humanitarian partners. As the Cluster Chair for Early Recovery under the Pacific Humanitarian Team, UNDP is spearheading a Housing and Building Damage Assessment initiative. This project aims to systematize reconstruction, strengthen local capacity, and enhance resilience, ensuring Vanuatu can better withstand future disasters.
